A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Misviz/Misviz-synth study, with readable main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–Q. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results in Table 2, manual error analysis, bounding-box evaluation, and an automatic-labeling pilot in Appendix G.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark experiments and reports a revised weak-labeling study with manual verification of 130 instances in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Appendix G revises the auxiliary labeling procedure by adding an EasyOCR readability filter and retaining only images with zero or one predicted misleader. The proposed linter, DePlot extractor, image-axis classifiers, and synthetic-chart generator remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same benchmark datasets, 12 misleader categories, chart domains, and detection tasks. Appendix G continues examining the same unlabeled collection from Lo et al.; its revised filtering and sample sizes concern existing coverage.

E2.justification: The same nine zero-shot MLLMs, two linter configurations, and two classifiers participate in Table 2. Appendix G still uses Qwen2.5-VL-72B; EasyOCR serves as preprocessing software, without becoming an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix G replaces a 1,000-image pilot with 100 manual checks with a filtered 4,053-instance corpus checked using 10 instances per label, reporting per-label precision. Section 3.1 changes the category-frequency cutoff from three to 15 instances. Appendix P changes its stated split from test to validation, matching the existing table caption; this does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: The existing dataset-scaling feasibility analysis is revised into a label-specific reliability audit, including examination of unreadable and educational images surviving selection. The other error analyses, localization study, subgroup breakdowns, and prompt-sensitivity analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both report one run for zero-shot MLLMs and classifier averages over seeds 123, 456, and 789, with identical standard deviations in v2 Table 8 and v3 Table 9. The revised manual audit adds no uncertainty intervals or significance testing.

E6.justification: Appendix G removes the pilot's 98% visualization-detection accuracy and its 20 binary-correct and 17 exact-correct outcomes among 41 identified charts. v3 Table 7 instead reports label-specific precision, including 100% for 3D, 90% for inconsistent tick intervals, and 0% for inappropriate use of line charts. These use different sampling conditions; the retained benchmark and appendix result tables are numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The category definitions, detection rules, and metric definitions retain their mathematical substance. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs, and the revised empirical audit introduces none.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same dataset contributions, proposed detectors, and central findings about real-world versus synthetic performance and limited generalization.

C2.justification: v2 broadly concludes that automatic annotation remains unreliable. v3 distinguishes potentially useful weak labels, such as 3D and inconsistent tick intervals, from unreliable categories, and explains that residual unreadable and educational images require further human verification.

D1.justification: v3 specifies EasyOCR, an average confidence threshold above 70, label-count filtering, and the visualization-detection prompt in Figure 13. It also updates the advertised repository address from arxiv2025-misviz to acl2026-misviz. Detector training details and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited research and comparative positioning are retained. MisVisFix remains the same work; replacing its placeholder year 5555 with 2026 and updating publication details are bibliographic corrections.

P1.justification: v3 makes scattered language corrections, reorders some category descriptions, updates acknowledgments, and rewrites Appendix G using weak-label terminology. The main narrative and Appendix A–Q structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the weak-label precision table as Table 7 and the visualization-detection prompt as Figure 13. Existing displays are renumbered and repositioned, including Figure 3 and several appendix tables and figures, while their visual content and formats are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix G provides more informative evidence about label reliability and clearer filtering and prompt details, improving the usefulness and reproducibility of the scaling analysis. Appendix P also resolves its test/validation wording conflict. The gains are limited by only 10 checks per label, removal of the earlier aggregate pilot measurements, and a remaining inconsistency between four selection criteria in Section 3.1 and three in Limitations.
